title: Twitch chat designs the games, an AI agent builds them on live stream
author: billy_bonus
selftext:
I run Lets Make Game, an experiment where nobody writes game code by hand.

How it works:

1. Viewers suggest ideas with `!idea` and vote with `!vote`. Any language works.
2. An autonomous coding agent builds the game live on stream: planning, coding, testing and fixing its own errors. You see the mistakes too.
3. The game is published as a free browser game. Viewers playtest it for an hour and report bugs, then the agent fixes them and republishes. That's up to six fix rounds per game.

17 games are published so far. The fastest coding session was 33 min 51 s with 28/28 tests passing. From idea to a playable game takes 80 minutes on median.

Curious what this sub thinks. How would you merge a dozen unrelated chat ideas into one coherent game spec without a human in the loop? Got any questions for me?

Stream: [www.twitch.tv/letsmakegame](https://www.twitch.tv/letsmakegame)  
Games: [letsmakegame.pages.dev](https://letsmakegame.pages.dev/)
